source_boundary.preserved_question_intent: Compare Java synchronized and ReentrantLock, including their shared locking semantics and the additional control exposed by ReentrantLock.

sources.title: Java Language Specification SE 21 — synchronized statement and monitor synchronization

claims.text: Both synchronized monitors and ReentrantLock are reentrant mutual-exclusion mechanisms: a thread may reacquire the same monitor/lock, with balanced unlock actions required before full release.

A synchronized statement automatically unlocks its monitor on normal or abrupt block completion, while Lock removes block-structured lifetime and therefore requires explicit unlock, conventionally in finally.

The Lock/ReentrantLock API exposes non-blocking tryLock, timed acquisition, interruptible acquisition and optional fair ordering, capabilities not exposed as equivalent controls by synchronized syntax.
ReentrantLock can be constructed with a fair policy, but fairness is a lock-admission property rather than JVM/OS scheduling fairness, and untimed tryLock does not honor the fairness setting.

Condition factors Object monitor wait/notify behavior into lock-associated condition objects and permits multiple distinct wait-sets for one Lock; await atomically releases and later reacquires the associated lock.

Successful Lock lock/unlock operations are required to provide the same memory synchronization effects as monitor lock/unlock; synchronized monitor unlock happens-before subsequent lock of the same monitor.

OpenJDK 21 implements ReentrantLock on AbstractQueuedSynchronizer, while synchronized monitor semantics are language-level contracts; implementation optimization details should not be promoted to cross-JVM language guarantees.

writer_constraints: Do not claim synchronized is non-reentrant; both mechanisms are reentrant.
Do not claim ReentrantLock is universally faster than synchronized; performance is workload/JDK dependent and is not the semantic distinction.
Distinguish ReentrantLock.lock() from lockInterruptibly(); only the latter is the explicit interruptible acquisition API.
State that synchronized automatically releases the monitor on normal or abrupt scope exit, while explicit Lock usage requires unlock in finally.
Preserve the fairness boundary: fair ReentrantLock is not scheduler fairness, and untimed tryLock() bypasses the fairness policy.
Do not present HotSpot monitor implementation details as Java language guarantees.
Do not fabricate project experience; the frozen repository packet contains comparison questions only.
